reviews.text: it's got its influences on its sleeve, but they're some good influences! you'll recognize a bit of every roguelite you love in here, but it's tuned up incredibly well. movement feels great, combat feels great, map building feels great! it's got challenges, it's got unlocks, it's great. fully recommend

Launch trailer explains it well enough so won't rehash the premise. She's a nice burger but light on condiments and fixin's currently. Seems to have been left wide open to future DLC and (hopefully) free content updates. Having said that the game does what it says and needs to do; no more, no less. I got this during it's introduction sale but standard US retail feels pretty spot on for what's here. Forty minutes in and I'm enjoying it as much as similar Rogue-Lites So thumbs up from me but it's still early game (and early days) so will update this recommendation if necessary.

I joined the playtest for this game. I can say, without reservation, this game is awesome! I have watched the game develop from just about the beginning, to my playtest time, and to where it is now. I have enjoyed every part of it! Combat is simple to understand, and items increase your abilities. The ability to lay out your path and choosing to push your limits, budget your resources, or work with penalties makes the challenge varied enough to keep playing. I am looking forward to seeing where else this goes, both with the gameplay itself and the story. If you are considering this but are on the fence, the sale should help. It is absolutely worth the full $15 asked, so the sale price is defintily something to take advantage of now.

Super fun rogue-lite that I can recommend for this price. Pros: - Combat is fluid - Room-building mechanic is innovative and works quite well - Super challenging but at the same time dying feels like it's my fault and not the game being cheap - Lots of stuff to upgrade Unsure: - Variety might not be there after playing a lot. There are not a lot of enemy types and bosses BUT there are a lot of items. Not sure what systems might unlock in the later stages of progression - Items might not be properly balance, many feel too weak. But maybe I haven't found the use case for those "weak" items yet that would make them strong Cons: - Story seems pretty basic but I'm only 3h in, maybe it picks up? But I also don't see story as a high priority in rogue-lite games - Sometimes the movement is a little bit floaty because of two reasons: 1) Attacking moves you forward a bit and 2) running or jumping towards a ledge automatically pulls you up even in battle

The game is really excellent, I've played a lot of rogue lite games and this one finally offers something new and refreshing. The fact that you can build your own path through the dungeon is really interesting and add a lot of depth to how you want to play and navigate in the dungeon. Combat also is very fluid and dynamic. The game is super pretty (i really love the artworks). Content-wise, it looks pretty solid, with plenty of challenges to complete. There is also many items and builds possibilities to create/unlock. I thinks that there's also plenty of "room" for further updates and dlcs. And on top of that, the game is really cheap, so go for it!

A very fluid and intuitive rouge-lite action plat former, there are obvious inspirations this game is leveraging from but in my opinion that is a good thing, we need more games like this, that take the best elements of other rouge-lite's and incorporate them in itself with a nice twist. Only the good stuff. The room building system is a neat mechanic that keeps things interesting, the whole curse dynamic makes you manage your resources carefully. Overall a very pleasant and fun game to play if you like these kinds of games, definitely recommend!

Excellent new rogue with a very funny mechanic that I haven't seen before. Being able to build rooms in the dungeon feels pretty great. I first thought it was cheating, but the game is well-balanced enough to make it challenging. The developers thought of backtracking — you can teleport to any previously visited room, and honestly, I feel that every rogue should have this kind of mechanic. The game feel is great, and there are tons of items to play with. I had many broken runs that felt really enjoyable. The art style and audio are also awesome. The game is beautiful, the music is entertaining, and the sounds are very satisfying. It’s a pretty damn good game on its own, but getting it for only 15 bucks is a real steal. Everyone should try this one!

tl;dr loving it so far! I've played only an hour or two but I can already tell that this thing has great bones. The combat is smooth, the enemies are fun to fight, and the room building mechanics I'm just getting started. The room building is fun so far, and you can make patterns to create different rooms such as health. I can tell there's a lot of solid metaprogression. I've only beaten a run two times, but each time there has been a new development in the story where you get harder enemies or unlocked challenge runs. Each run is about 20 minutes for me and when I beat a run last time it put me into a completely new area. I'll update when I do a couple runs in there with regards to enemy variety and such. The only thing slightly lacking are perhaps the upgrades as there haven't been too many interesting ones yet, and I think there's only one weapon type. I think there could be room for content updates with regards to combat. But that's really the only thoughts I have so far. It feels great to play, platforming is just fine, and I hope for more content updates in the future.

Can you believe it? You're building your own dungeon! You are the [h2][b]Game Master! [/b][/h2] The biggest thing about this dungeon crawler is.. you don't just crawl, you build it yourself! It's up to you if you get a path with healing item or bridge to reach next shopkeeper or reach the boss! The controls are very nice and responsive, both on keyboard and controller which is welcome surprise despite it being a platformer.[spoiler] I hate lantern enemy... [/spoiler] Game offers plenty of items and choices that can make your run a breeze or pain in the blueprint.. You have to mind your resources while architecting or else you will get hit with a nasty curse that plugs your ears with some loose cotton bud. Unless you got something that boosts your efficiency with these curses hehe. Good game definitely recommend if you love rougelikes that shake the things around from other games alike!
画风精美，玩法创新，手感堪比死亡细胞的好，玩就对了，神作！ （可惜了不咋出名，怎么评价这么少）

2D action roguelike with fluid, Dead Cells-y combat, mysterious environments, great sound design & the ability to create your own map, making the dungeon crawling aspect really interesting. Very cool! EDIT: After playing for a while longer, I'm noticing the skill ceiling feels artifically cranked. Beating the first boss and unlocking the second level adds harder enemies, more traps, etc to the first level, which makes it feel like I'll never actually see the second level I just unlocked, let alone the first boss. Losing runs over and over to slowly grind away at upgrades that don't really effect my run at all isn't making me want to come back either.

It's a shame that I can't recommend this game mechanically it is well done, but the amount of bad balance completely overshadows any and all sense of fun this game could be offering. Well lets start with the good. 1. Movement feels fluid and responsive. 2. While the combat is nothing more than basically button mashing it is still kinda fun since you position matters somewhat. 3. Decent variety of enemies and rooms. 4. Decent meta progression with impactful talents. 5. Fun little site challenges that you can do to unlock new items for future runs. 6. Being able to build your own path is a fun little twist of the genre, could use a bit more room variety though. So now on to the bad. 1: The most important problem by far is the fact that enemies, and especially bosses, are just way too tanky and have too much health after act 1. This not only completely ruins the flow of the game by having you spend way too much time button mashing a single enemy, it also just stretches your average run by a lot. It's a shame since Act 1 feels amazing to play. The game only has 3 acts or "biomes" and that is ok, no need to stretch the run length artificially by making every enemy take ages to defeat. 2: Bosses are too hard because of their insane amounts of health. This is more of an extension of the first point, but bosses in this game are straight-up unfun to fight against thanks to their massive health pool, which gets coupled with the fact that half of the time you can't even hit them because they are either out of your range or are doing some attack that forces you to get away from them. The attacks they do are mostly fine and can be dodged after a bit of learning, but the health is just over the top, it turns bosses into more of a DPS check rather than a skill check. 3: Most items are straight-up garbage/not impactful, or just boring. While the game has many different items, most of them are way too situational or just bad and don't make you feel much stronger. It's a shame when some of the best items in the game are simple stat ups like "10% more weapon damage" and stuff like that. I also think that this is a reason why it takes so long to even kill basic enemies since there are very few ways of actually increasing your damage throughout a run. In a game like this, you need items that not only make you stronger but also change the way you play in any given run, while here I sometimes don't even notice I have certain items since they are just so niche or situational. Which in turn makes every run feel the same. While it looks like the good outweighs the bad, the bad is so impactful to the overall fun and flow of the game that I just can't see myself playing this any further. All this game needs is a big balance pass over most of the items and health scaling, and then you have a decent game. Until then, I can't recommend the game.

[b] [u]TLDR :[/u] [/b] this would be a great 0.01 Early Access release. Except it's supposedly the finished product. Unbalanced & unfinished. ------------------------------------------- [b] [u]Blabla :[/u] [/b] it looks good & the core mechanics are good. But the tuning / balancing of hero / items / enemies is godawful. Also lacks some basic stuff that gives it a strong unfinished vibe. ( no dialogue sounds, main menu is a cheap ugly screenshot ) No sense of progress or improvement at all since I hit the 2h mark. Just getting punished / fighting a losing battle over & over. No doubt it's partially skill issue, but I've finished quite a few roguelites. Now 4 hours in I am entirely tuned out / ready to uninstall. Then it got bad. Here's hoping they stick with it / improve it, it *could* be great. Happy to give it another chance when / if they rebalance / improve.

这是一款横板肉鸽动作游戏。 游戏的画面还算可以吧，建模还算精细，角色和怪物都看着有点美式万圣节风格，就是场景略显重复，总体来说算是中等偏上的水准。 背景设定好像是玩家是造物主，然后被自己的仆人召唤回了自己曾经建造的小世界，但是这个世界已经被新生的造物主占据，然后玩家要做的就是打败新造物主，夺回这个小世界的控制权。 玩法上有肉鸽元素，不过主要的的玩法还是横板动作。 游戏的特色在于，玩家可以消耗资源自己随意摆放各种房间来进行连接，然后在探索自己摆放的房间（敌人，商店，回血等），直到连接到boss房，打倒boss后就算完成了。 内容还是挺多的，虽然武器不能更换，但是遗物就有大几十种，相互配合之后，打起来看着比较花哨。 战斗手感还是相当不错的，主角非常灵活，闪避不仅动作灵敏，还能再攻击中使用，无敌帧也很长。 有局外养成和收集，手机部分有点死亡细胞的既视感，而养成部分虽然不能让角色战斗力直接变高，但是能让玩家在局内资源获取和容错率上增加很多。 顺带一提，如果想要当叮达人，局外资源是单浮点，局内则是四字节--我略施小计，用一排商店连接到了boss，然后无限走商店买各种遗物，去了boss房5秒不到就把boss干掉了（狗头）。 有中文，但是翻译的水平有点机翻，然后还有各种专属名词是英语。 总体来说还是个挺有意思的动作肉鸽游戏，内容丰富，战斗手感非常不错，喜欢动作肉鸽的话还是非常推荐尝试本作的。 [quote]游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见[/quote]

Overall I like this game, but after 11 hours I'm not sure how much more I'll play. The good -Fast, fluid and responsive movement. I've played an insane amount of Dead Cells on Switch and felt at home jumping and dodging here. This game just feels good to control. -Building out the rooms is a cool idea and has some neat trade offs with the curses. Also really appreciate being able to just teleport instantly between rooms you've cleared. -I love the gothic art and character design. Animations look good too--you'll see the three hit combo a gazillion times, but it looks cool! The dice is a unique weapon. -Bonus trials are a nice addition and some of them present some tough challenges. -Some really cool upgrades like the echo dice that show up on dash or enemy death. -I like Bernardo and his costumes and his absolute refusal to break character. The bad -The structure of the game is in three acts (each with its own biome). After you complete an act, stronger enemies (as well as enemies from that new biome) will show up in act 1. The boss from act 1 will also be stronger, and will have new attacks and patterns. This is a neat idea in theory as it makes the early levels you have to run through again feel a little fresh, but the new enemies are damage sponges. Before it might have taken 15 minutes to get to the act 1 boss, but now its double that time. Once you've unlocked act 3, you'll face even stronger versions of enemies in act 1 and 2, and their life bars are enormous. Just getting through rooms feels like a slog, and most runs you feel under powered, even with all your potential upgrades. The act 2 boss after unlocking act 3 becomes a frustrating chore to fight, and takes so long to get to that dying makes you hover over the uninstall button. Feels like it might have been better to make the enemies easier in act 1 and 2 after you've cleared them, and just throw in more challenging boss patterns or room types or something, maybe more risk/reward with how you build the dungeon. This game goes from "Dang I died...I'm gonna try just one more run!" to "Ugh I died...I think I'll stop playing now, or maybe stop playing forever." -Would have been cool to have more weapon variety or maybe elemental effects that interact with each other. Maybe even ways the dice could transform for new animations. Like maybe the dice multiplies into several small dice forming a whip and your three hit combo becomes a fast six hit combo. Or your dice grows and looks like a sledgehammer, giving you a slow and strong two hit combo. I'm a thumbs up overall because I enjoyed my time playing this over the past week between my desktop and steam deck (it runs okay enough), and if there are updates, I'll definitely jump back in. It's sorta like Destiny 1, the base level gameplay, the fundamentals, are really solid. With the right improvements I'd enthusiastically recommend, but for now, consider the caveats above!

I don't like leaving negative reviews, would rather refund the game though have played for too long so can't. I really wanted to like this however it way, way too 'samey'. 4 hours into it I am still replaying the exact same levels when I started playing it. First off, it looks good and the devs obviously put a lot of work into it, though definitely not for me. The idea is a good one however I think there is a lot missing from it to make it work properly, yes you can arrange rooms which is great however the rooms are all incredibly similar so it is like a 4 piece puzzle. Yes, it is a puzzle, though doesn't take very long to get bored. There are very few enemy types in the first area and you can learn their moves within an hour which makes the area very easy. Then you must grind to the 1st boss every time you replay and the 1st boss takes A LOT of hits to reduce the HP. It is damn easy to get to the 1st boss once you have learned the few enemy moves then too damn difficult and long to kill the 1st boss (I have given up). Also, the items/powerups are very limited and seem to make only minor differences to gameplay. I can reach the 1st boss with any combination of items very easily making them seem worthless. I really think a bit more imagination could have been put into the item effects. Weapon upgrades are incredibly dull and limited, it doesn't feel 'really cool' to upgrade to your weapon as it looks and behaves almost identically as before. Some people will like it, though I think the concept could have been taken much further and it would have been an amazing game. Currently it is (to me) below average, like the devs had an amazing idea when they started and then ran of steam and just stopped adding to it, which is a shame.

Seeing all the complaints about bosses being absurdly tanky, the game being completely unbalanced, and leveling-up items feeling useless, I figured I’d reach out to the developers about this half-baked disaster. But, of course, they’re either too busy or just don’t care enough to respond—let alone fix their broken mess. So thanks for nothing—I absolutely love being stuck at the first boss over and over again. As a dedicated roguelike fan, I wish I could recommend this game, but I just can’t.

Very cute premise, but combat feels ass because dodging is ass. What I mean is that, yes, you *technically* have I-frames on your dodge, but those only last way too little to actually dodge through any attack, and your main purpose of the dodge is to instead get out of whatever attack is heading your way. There is no way to elegantly make use of understanding enemy attack timings, and as such, it makes you feel like you're actively fighting against a combat system that absolutely wants you to play like a scaredy cat or die. That is not a very good thing to have in a roguelike like this where every bit of health is annoyingly precious to you as the player, and it really makes runs feel very drawn out and bothersome because you have no agency over the hitboxes or attack timings. All you can do is use your dashes to get out of the way. This is further exacerbated by having enemies that literally force you to stay away from them to avoid their attacks, which is just an annoying way to introduce downtime in its combat system. Hell, the game is hardly even subtle about it, since several of the weapon upgrades amount to "you dont actually swing with your weapon, but instead place it in the air where it continues to damage the enemy", so you just leave your weapon wherever the enemy will be and then get as far away as you can. Amazing.

自主构建地牢房间、路线，策略性的选择奖励、挑战，不能否认这一核心机制十分新颖而有趣 但是作为一款动作肉鸽，我的战斗体验并不有趣 1.无用、无趣的遗物，两个小时的游玩中，未碰见有趣的机制类遗物或者机制和数值类遗物带来的提升都非常小，以至于很难感受到奖励的正向反馈 2.战斗全靠基础动作模组及玩家的技术强撑，且相较孱弱的遗物，精英敌人和boss的血量都挺厚的，难度并不低 整体体验下来，并不像在玩肉鸽，而是在玩一款难度不低的横版动作（boss战挺有趣，但死亡后又得无趣且耗时的经过道中环节令人烦躁） 2小时的游戏时间 还有大量的关卡和遗物未解锁 作出的评价可能会有失偏颇 但实在没有动力再继续坐牢了

I'm quite disappointed by the full game, after the decent demo and in its current state, I can definitely not recommend it. Maybe after the devs did some serious rebalancing of all aspects (including the room placement) I would second bastie2606's review to 100%.

I enjoyed the first few runs, but things started falling flat after defeating the first boss. Item variety is limited, with many of them being flat stat buffs or otherwise not being especially interesting or impactful, while a few are game-changers that are a total crapshoot to get (most notably the ones that make your attack hover in place and hit things nearby while you can just dodge). Enemy variety is also limited, combat gets repetitive, your dodge could be a lot more useful, and things get a bit unreasonable with the the enemy upgrades after being the first boss (who isn't much better, as good luck attacking them without getting hit unless you have one of the aforementioned sentry gun items). And even the mapbuilding that's the game's unique gimmick isn't that interesting; it just periodically interrupts fighting with putting an enemy cell (or whatever else you may need) wherever leads to the next generated group of cells. Doesn't seem to be as deep as intended.

Very meh game. It's just boring, and makes such poor use of the roguelike system. The "upgrades" you get are so bland and uninspired, and anything remotely interesting comes with downsides. It's like the devs are scared an upgrade might actually make you capable of killing something in fewer than 8 hits. This doesn't seem like it should be a roguelike game, and instead you should just acquire upgrades as you go. But replaying the same boring levels over and over is not exciting. I can play Slay the Spire, Hades, Binding of Isaac, or Balatro for days. I could barely stomach 3 hours of this game.

Cryptical Path is an action roguelite developed by Old Skull Games and published by Old Skull Games together with Game Seer that combines dungeon crawling, strategic planning, and fast-paced combat into a formula that feels both recognizable and refreshingly different. While many games in the genre rely heavily on random generation and adaptation, Cryptical Path introduces mechanics that place more control directly into the player's hands. The result is an experience that rewards not only combat skill but also thoughtful decision-making, creating a roguelite adventure where planning ahead becomes just as important as surviving the next encounter. Set within a dangerous prison known as the Hexium, players step into the role of the Architect, an entity connected to the labyrinth itself and tasked with reclaiming control over a world that has fallen into chaos. Once designed as a containment structure for dark and powerful forces, the prison has become unstable, corrupted by the very dangers it was built to suppress. Ancient threats move freely through its halls, hidden dangers wait behind forgotten pathways, and the deeper players travel, the more they uncover about both the prison and the role of the Architect within its history. One of the strongest ideas behind Cryptical Path revolves around dungeon construction. Instead of entering completely randomized levels and adapting purely through reaction, players actively influence progression by choosing which rooms appear during a run. Shops, combat challenges, healing opportunities, and progression routes become strategic decisions rather than entirely random outcomes. This mechanic adds an extra layer of control that significantly changes how runs develop. That system creates an experience where long-term planning matters constantly. Building a path through the dungeon involves balancing immediate survival against future opportunities. Safer routes may preserve resources but limit rewards. More dangerous paths may offer stronger upgrades while introducing greater risks. The game consistently encourages players to evaluate consequences before committing to decisions, creating tension that extends beyond combat itself. Combat serves as another major highlight. Movement feels responsive, encounters move quickly, and survival often depends on maintaining momentum rather than approaching enemies cautiously. Combat design rewards positioning, awareness, and proper timing while keeping encounters energetic throughout progression. Enemies pressure players aggressively, demanding adaptation and precision as challenges gradually become more difficult. The movement systems contribute heavily to the game's overall pacing. Dodging attacks, repositioning during battles, and maintaining control over chaotic encounters creates satisfying combat flow that remains engaging even across repeated runs. The faster combat style works especially well alongside the strategic dungeon-building systems because it ensures gameplay remains active rather than overly methodical. Progression systems outside individual runs also strengthen long-term engagement. Permanent upgrades and unlockable improvements ensure failed attempts still contribute toward future success. Strong roguelites often succeed by making defeat feel like part of growth rather than punishment, and Cryptical Path handles this aspect effectively. Every run offers opportunities to learn, improve strategies, and gradually build stronger capabilities for future attempts. Replay value naturally becomes one of the game's strongest qualities. Since players actively shape progression routes themselves, repeated runs rarely feel identical. Different choices produce different pacing, different opportunities, and different challenges. Experimentation becomes part of the appeal rather than simply optimizing one ideal strategy repeatedly. Visually, Cryptical Path embraces a darker fantasy presentation that supports its atmosphere effectively. The Hexium feels dangerous and mysterious while maintaining visual clarity during combat-heavy moments. Environmental design reinforces the oppressive nature of the prison setting without sacrificing gameplay readability. Enemy designs and visual effects contribute further to immersion while helping maintain tension throughout progression. The darker narrative themes also help strengthen identity. While gameplay remains the primary focus, the setting and story elements create additional motivation to continue exploring deeper into the prison. Uncovering hidden details surrounding the world and its history adds meaning beyond progression systems alone. The experience does present occasional limitations. Some players may find certain progression elements stronger than others, occasionally narrowing experimentation during longer sessions. Combat pacing can also fluctuate depending on upgrades and encounter structure. However, these issues rarely overshadow the systems that make the game stand out. What ultimately makes Cryptical Path memorable is how confidently it challenges genre expectations. Rather than allowing randomness to dictate every outcome, it introduces player agency directly into progression systems. Success depends not only on quick reactions but also on planning, route management, and understanding long-term consequences. Cryptical Path succeeds because it recognizes that replayability comes from meaningful decisions just as much as procedural variation. The combination of strategic dungeon construction, satisfying combat systems, and rewarding progression creates an experience that feels distinctive inside a crowded genre. Cryptical Path delivers strong action gameplay, smart strategic systems, and excellent replay value while introducing fresh ideas that help separate it from more conventional roguelite experiences. Rating: 8/10

Its a somewhat unique concept for the genre, I'll give it that. It falls short in just about everything else. There is not enough variation to keep the gameplay loop engaging and I found the game fizzled out quickly. They should have taken a cue from games like Spiritfall and incorporated different weapons at minimum. Each act ends in the same boss every run. The artifacts found are dull, unexciting and lack synergy. The talent tree is 1-dimensional and predictable. I found the value would have been more appropriate at 10-15$ and could probably be relegated to a mobile game.
